passage.title: Modest Threads
paras: Modest Threads is a small UK modest-wear brand. It designs abayas, long dresses and hijabs and sews them in its own workshop of 12 staff. It sells through its own website and two market stalls.
Last year 30% of its online orders came from abroad: the USA, Malaysia and the Gulf. Delivery abroad takes 6 to 10 days.

New online brands from other countries now sell similar abayas for about £10 less. Fabric costs have risen. The owner is thinking about having the sewing done by a factory in Turkey, which would cut the cost of each abaya from £22 to £14.
passage.source: All businesses, people and figures in this case are fictional, made up for practice.

head: Modest Threads
Last year
rows: Cost of making one in the UK workshop

blocks.text: Analyse one threat globalisation poses to Modest Threads.

questions.q: Stretch: should Modest Threads move its sewing to Turkey? Give one point for and one against.
questions.a: For: cost per abaya falls from £22 to £14, so it can match rivals' prices or raise its margin. Against: less control over quality and ethical standards, longer lead times, and 12 UK jobs at risk.

markScheme.a: For example: foreign online brands sell similar abayas for about £10 less (evidence), so Modest Threads may have to cut its £50 price or lose sales; with costs of £22 and rising fabric prices its margin falls (chain); therefore globalisation increases competition and threatens profit (link).
